```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(linregpkg)
library(caret)
library(mlbench)
data("BostonHousing")
```

## 1. Training and test data

We use 80 % of the observations for training and 20 % for testing.

```{r}
set.seed(12345)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(BostonHousing$medv, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- BostonHousing[train_idx, ]
test_data  <- BostonHousing[-train_idx, ]
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)
```

## 2. Linear regression and forward selection

```{r}
lm_fit <- train(medv ~ ., data = train_data, method = "lm", trControl = ctrl)

# 13 covariates -> allow models with 1, ..., 13 covariates
fwd_fit <- train(medv ~ ., data = train_data, method = "leapForward",
                 tuneGrid = data.frame(nvmax = 1:13), trControl = ctrl)
fwd_fit$results[, c("nvmax", "RMSE", "Rsquared")]
fwd_fit$bestTune
```

The table above shows that cross-validation compares models with 1 up to all
13 covariates (if `tuneGrid` is not given, caret only tries `nvmax` = 2, 3, 4,
which does not satisfy the requirement). The intercept-only model (0 covariates) is not part of the
`leapForward` grid, so we compare it by hand: its RMSE is simply the standard
deviation of `medv`, which is much larger than for any of the models above.

```{r}
sd(train_data$medv)
```

## 3. Performance on the training data

```{r}
rmse <- function(y, yhat) sqrt(mean((y - yhat)^2))
data.frame(
  model = c("lm", "forward selection"),
  train_RMSE = c(rmse(train_data$medv, predict(lm_fit, train_data)),
                 rmse(train_data$medv, predict(fwd_fit, train_data)))
)
```

## 4–5. Ridge regression, tuning lambda with 10-fold CV

`ridgereg_caret()` makes our `ridgereg()` usable as a custom caret model.

```{r}
ridge_fit <- train(medv ~ ., data = train_data, method = ridgereg_caret(),
                   tuneGrid = data.frame(lambda = seq(0, 30, by = 1)),
                   trControl = ctrl)
ridge_fit$bestTune
plot(ridge_fit)
```

## 6. Performance on the test data

```{r}
test_res <- data.frame(
  model = c("lm", "forward selection", "ridgereg"),
  test_RMSE = c(rmse(test_data$medv, predict(lm_fit, test_data)),
                rmse(test_data$medv, predict(fwd_fit, test_data)),
                rmse(test_data$medv, predict(ridge_fit, test_data)))
)
test_res
```

## Conclusions

The three models give similar test RMSE. Forward selection uses fewer
covariates, and ridge regression shrinks the coefficients towards zero; with
only 13 covariates and more than 400 observations there is little
overfitting, so the optimal penalty is small and the gain from ridge
regression over ordinary least squares is modest.
